title: Pay-for-Performance Facebook Ads Agencies and Their Pricing
summary: Compare pay-for-performance Facebook ads agencies by fee model, percentage of spend, minimums and guarantees, and check what counts as a result before you sign.
body_markdown:
Knowlify is our top pick if you want money back when ads do not pay: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Other published models are a percentage of ad spend (Adside AI, WebFX, Pinprick, Growthr), a retainer with performance incentives (Pilothouse), a revenue partnership (KlientBoost) and a production fee tied to results (TubeScience). Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What does pay-for-performance mean in practice?


Three structures get called performance pricing, and each shifts risk differently. A percentage of spend ties the fee to how much you put behind ads, not to what the ads return. A retainer with a performance incentive pays a base fee plus a bonus when targets are met. A pay-for-performance production deal pays for ads that perform, rather than for production. Ask which structure is on the table before you compare numbers.


Percentage models are the most common in the published pricing here.[Adside AI](https://www.adside.ai/pricing) lists 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum for its managed service.[WebFX](https://www.webfx.com/social-media/services/advertising/) lists its Pro ongoing fee as the greater of $975 or 15% of ad spend, plus a separate $1,975 initial campaign investment in month one. In both cases, the fee grows with spend, and the floor decides the cost at small budgets.


## Which providers publish performance-linked terms?


Use this section as a shortlist of models to ask about, not as a ranking.


### Knowlify: our top pick for a refund if the ads do not pay back


If you want performance to carry real risk for the agency, a money-back term is the simplest test, and it is what Knowlify offers: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). Managed plans carry an agreed target in 30 days instead. Around that term sit about 25 finished ads a week, a first batch on day 5 so the 90 days go to testing rather than waiting, a person checking every ad, and three formats (AI UGC, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials). You can add end-to-end Meta management or buy creative only. Pricing is a custom quote with no public rate card. Pick another option if you want a published fee formula or a fee that rises and falls with spend or revenue, because ours is a refund term on a custom quote.


### TubeScience: pay for ads that perform


[TubeScience](https://tubescience.com/) describes a pay-for-performance production model and also advertises media buying. Its rates are not published, and its FAQ says teams not prepared to scale spend to seven figures monthly may be a weaker fit, while noting exceptions. Ask about eligibility, payment triggers and testing obligations before you assume a performance-linked fee is a low-commitment pilot.


### Adside AI: 10% of spend with a monthly floor


Its managed service lists 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum. The one fee covers strategy, creative production, launch, optimization and reporting. The page does not say how many creatives the fee includes, so that is a question to put in writing.


### WebFX: the greater of a floor or a percentage


Its Pro ongoing fee is the greater of $975 or 15% of ad spend. That structure is different from Adside AI's flat percentage, so compare both at the same monthly spend before you decide.


### Pinprick: no per-ad fee, production paid as a percentage


[Pinprick](https://pinprick.io/pricing) says eligible brands, mainly those already spending meaningfully on ads, pay no per-ad fee. Production is paid as an agreed percentage of ad spend, the rate is not published, and media buying is scoped separately. Its agency page also headlines ten UGC ads for $2,000 with no conditions listed, so ask which pricing applies to you.


### Growthr: a retainer plus a share of managed media


[Growthr](https://growthr.com/creative-production/) charges $10,000 a month plus a flat 10% of managed media spend, alongside paid media on every channel, analytics and attribution. No weekly ad count or contract length is published.


### Pilothouse: retainers with performance incentives


[Pilothouse](https://www.pilothouse.co/) prices through monthly retainers, performance-based incentives and custom project scopes. It is built for established DTC ecommerce brands, and no minimum spend is published.


### KlientBoost: a revenue partnership option


[KlientBoost](https://www.klientboost.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) lists a revenue partnership among its five ways to work together, next to ongoing management, audits, setup and consulting. Its fee is not published, and it works with ad budgets from $5,000 a month. A revenue-linked deal needs the same clause work described below.


## Do the numbers work at your spend level?


Percentage and minimum models change shape with the budget. At $20,000 of monthly spend, Adside AI's 10% is $2,000, so its $3,500 minimum applies. At $50,000, 10% is $5,000, which is above that minimum. WebFX's greater-of structure crosses over at $6,500: below that spend the $975 floor applies, and at $20,000 its 15% would be $3,000. These are our calculations from the published terms, not quotes.


Each calculation excludes media. Meta's[ad pricing page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/pricing) says the advertiser sets a daily or lifetime budget, so a fee of 10% of spend sits on top of the money you put behind ads. Meta's[minimum budgets help page](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) says Ads Manager requires a minimum budget that varies by country and objective, and shows an alert when a budget is too low. The same page says that with a cost per result goal, your daily budget should be at least five times that goal. That matters if a contract ties fees to a target cost per acquisition: as an illustration, a $40 target implies at least $200 a day.
